assumptions: at least five chain links are reachable via +0x20 from *(rsi)
the BSS tag string at 0x6508800 is initialized before the call; its bytes are not in the file and are not claimed
the global at 0x64ecf80 holds 0x5d4d490 after relocation, per the single RELATIVE record

caller.rule: calls 0x606ca40 on (rsi + 0x20) first; when *(rbx + 0x60) is non-null it writes the header (11, 0, 0) into the owner and skips the notify; when null it allocates a 0x30-byte subobject with _Znwm, builds it with 0x61bc290, stores it at *(rbx + 0x60) with byte *(rbx + 0x68) = 1, then calls 0x61bca30(owner, subobject) exactly once; afterwards it calls 0x60d52f0 on (rsi + 0x20) and returns the owner
caller.unpinned_callees: 0x606ca40, 0x61bc290 and 0x60d52f0 are recorded only at their call sites; their bodies are not pinned in this packet

chain_walk.precondition_assumption: at least five links are reachable via +0x20 from *(rsi); the routine never checks for a null link
chain_walk.return_value: saved at rsp+0x50 and framed by 0x61b1260; the slot target is virtual and not pinned to one address
rule: slot(head) compared against *(0x64ecf80); on mismatch call slot(head) with (head, rsi, rbx=&message)
then link1 = *(head + 0x20): slot(link1) compared against slot(head); on mismatch call slot(link1)
then link2, link3 the same pairwise way
then link4 = *(link3 + 0x20): its slot is called unconditionally, with (link4, rsi, rbx=&message)

cleanup.canary: stack protector at rsp+0x98, checked on the normal path and in every length-error and landing-pad arm; failure calls __stack_chk_fail
cleanup.landing_pads: 0x61bcd42 and 0x61bcd4e jump into the shared cleanup fragment 0x61bc9f6..0x61bca28, which disposes both strings via _M_dispose, checks the canary and resumes unwinding with _Unwind_Resume
cleanup.normal_path: the framed string is freed by sized delete of (data, size + 1) unless its data is its own SSO buffer at rsp+0x40; the message string is freed the same way unless its data is its own SSO buffer at rsp+0x78; then the canary at rsp+0x98 is checked and the owner is returned

delivery.arguments: rdi = owner, rsi = the +0x28 object, rdx = pointer to a {data, size} view of the framed string (data at rsp+0x40 SSO buffer or heap, size at rsp+0x38)
delivery.slot_target: virtual and not pinned to one address

expected_slot_walker.role: the default slot-0x98 handler the chain is compared against; it is what the homogeneous path resolves to
expected_slot_walker.rule: starts at *(rdi + 0x20), walks eight pairwise slot comparisons, tail-jumps to the first differing link's slot function, or to the ninth link's slot function when all eight comparisons pass; no stack frame, no return

frame.layout: raw 8 bytes of the return value || one flag byte (1) || LE32(len(message)) || message bytes
frame.length_guards: each append requires its length <= 0x3fffffffffffffff - size, else __throw_length_error with "basic_string::append"; the final whole-message append is a tail jump to _M_append
frame.value_block_at: rsp+0x50: qword = slot-call return value, byte +0x08 = 1, qword +0x10 = 0, message string at +0x18

inferences: the +0x20 chain with per-link slot-0x98 handlers reads as a handler chain of one handler kind per link; the name of that kind is not in the binary

the message (varint length-prefixed tag plus LE32 8 and LE32 1) reads as a framed record, and the 0x61b1260 output reads as a second framing (value, flag, length, payload); the record names are not in the binary
the slot-0x98 function is read as taking (link, context, out-string) from the registers live at the call sites; its name and return meaning are not pinned

message.length_guards: each append requires the appended length <= 0x3fffffffffffffff - size, else __throw_length_error with "basic_string::append" (string at 0x4474d2); the two 4-byte appends require remaining capacity >= 4
message.string_at: rsp+0x68 (std::string: data +0x00, size +0x08, SSO buffer at rsp+0x78)
message.tag_global: 0x6508800 (std::string: data +0x00, size +0x08) in BSS; bytes not retained in the file
message.varint_encoder: 0x61bd410 (FDE 0x61bd410..0x61bd4e9): ULEB128 of a u32 into rdi, returns the end pointer; 1 byte to 0x7f, 2 to 0x3fff, 3 to 0x1fffff, 4 to 0xfffffff, 5 above

inputs.rdi: owner, kept in r12 and returned in rax on the normal path
inputs.rsi: subobject; *(rsi) is the chain head, *(rsi + 0x28) is the delivery target

routine.returns: owner (rdi) on the normal path; the two landing pads at 0x61bcd42 and 0x61bcd4e resume unwinding instead
